newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Embattled Karabakh enclave votes for president.
newsitem.headline: Embattled Karabakh enclave votes for president.

text.p: The mostly ethnic Armenian population of Azerbaijan's embattled enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh went to the polls on Sunday in a presidential election which the current regional leader is expected to win.

An uneasy ceasefire has held in the mountainous region since May 1994, six years after it declared independence from Azerbaijan. Thousands of Moslem Azeris displaced from the area in the fighting were reported to have demonstrated over the weekend in Azerbaijan in protest at the holding of the election.
Local journalists in the Nagorno-Karabakh capital Stepanakert, contacted by telephone from the Armenian capital Yerevan, said voting had gone smoothly.
By the close of polls at 1700 GMT, 76 percent of the electorate of 89,000 had cast their ballots, electoral officials said. The results were expected on Monday.

Western countries have joined Azeri President Haydar Aliyev in condemning the vote, saying it could jeopardise peace talks involving Armenia and Azerbaijan. Karabakh makes no secret of its desire to join Armenia. Azerbaijan refuses to consider anything more than autonomy for the region.

Robert Kocharyan, who two years ago was elected president of the self-declared republic, is widely expected to win a new, five-year mandate. Standing against him are Boris Arushayan and communist leader Grant Melkumyan.
The fighting, in which mainly Christian ethnic Armenians drove Azeris out and set the former Soviet states of Armenia and Azerbaijan at loggerheads, claimed over 10,000 lives.
On Friday, Armenia and Azerbaijan failed again to agree on resolving the conflict after talks in Helsinki.
